title: Agent Network Topology and Safety: Do Some Communication Topologies Produce More Safety Failures Than Others?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If topology affects safety, it provides a design-time intervention. However, the causal chain is less direct: real multi-agent systems often use task-determined topologies, limiting the practical applicability of topology choice as a safety lever.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing 4 different multi-agent topologies each running 30 tasks with a 5-agent system is a substantial engineering challenge. Beginners would need significant infrastructure setup. The combinatorial scale (4 topologies x 30 tasks x 5 agents) requires non-trivial orchestration code.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 4 topologies x 30 tasks is 120 experimental runs, each involving 5 coordinating agents. This is far too large for 30 hours. Even scoped to 2 topologies and 10 tasks, the multi-agent infrastructure alone would consume most of the time budget.
